GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production change with no tests, fewer than 4 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these):
  server/pipeline/clip_judge.py
  tests/test_clip_min_count.py
  tests/test_clip_judge.py

THE PROBLEM, measured on a real episode. The owner asked "did you generate 3 viral social clips?" The pipeline shipped ONE. server/pipeline/clip_judge.py declares MIN_CLIPS = 3 and CONFIDENCE_FLOOR = 0.8, but the floor is enforced as an ALL-OR-NOTHING per-pick gate: validation raises ClipJudgeRefusal on the FIRST pick whose confidence is below 0.8 (see the `conf < CONFIDENCE_FLOOR` raise). Two real outcomes both fail the owner:
  * A previous run: "all 3 pick(s) below confidence floor 0.8" -> total refusal, caller fell back to heuristic picks.
  * The current run: the judge returned exactly ONE pick at confidence 0.84 out of a pool of 8 candidates, and nothing objected. The manifest recorded expected_count=1, validated_count=1, ok=true. MIN_CLIPS was never enforced on the OUTPUT COUNT, so shipping a single clip looked like success.

THE FIX — always deliver MIN_CLIPS, ranked, with confidence preserved and weak picks flagged rather than dropped:
1. Stop raising on a single below-floor pick. Validate STRUCTURE strictly as now (grounded timestamps, length between MIN_LEN_S and MAX_LEN_S, required fields, no invented content) — a structurally invalid pick is still a refusal. But treat confidence as a RANKING signal, not a per-pick veto.
2. After structural validation, sort surviving picks by confidence descending and return the top `num_clips`. Mark each pick `below_floor: true/false` against CONFIDENCE_FLOOR and carry its confidence through unchanged so downstream can surface weak clips for human review.
3. Enforce a genuine OUTPUT FLOOR: if the number of structurally valid picks is fewer than min(MIN_CLIPS, num_clips), raise ClipJudgeRefusal naming how many were valid versus required, so the caller's heuristic fallback engages instead of silently shipping a thin set. Shipping fewer than the floor must be impossible without a loud refusal.
4. Add a module-level summary on the returned value (or a second return element if the current contract allows it without breaking callers — inspect the real signature and keep it backward compatible): how many picks were below floor, so the caller can queue a review card. Do NOT change the caller; another lane owns that.
5. Keep CONFIDENCE_FLOOR and MIN_CLIPS as the named constants they are, with comments recording that the floor now ranks and flags rather than vetoing, and citing the real single-clip incident.

TESTS (tests/test_clip_min_count.py, pure with mocked model output; at least 4): (1) three picks with confidences 0.84/0.62/0.55 all return, sorted descending, the lower two flagged below_floor=true; (2) NEGATIVE: only two structurally valid picks when three are required raises ClipJudgeRefusal, and the message names 2 and 3 — proving a thin set cannot ship silently; (3) a structurally invalid pick (ungrounded timestamp or length outside MIN_LEN_S..MAX_LEN_S) is still refused even at confidence 0.99; (4) num_clips smaller than MIN_CLIPS is honoured (asking for 1 does not raise when 1 valid pick exists); (5) confidences are preserved unchanged on the returned picks. Keep existing clip_judge tests green; if one asserts the old all-or-nothing refusal, UPDATE it with a one-line comment citing the single-clip incident.

Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Create a NEW module. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 5 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these — create both):
  server/pipeline/content_mechanics.py
  tests/test_content_mechanics_gate.py

WHY. The podcast's generated copy keeps failing a human voice reviewer on MECHANICAL faults that no code checks: 40+ word run-on sentences, zero contractions, stacked calls-to-action, self-answered rhetorical questions, invented statistics, banned corporate words, and identical sentences reused across posts. The owner's own approved show-notes summary ends with a 44-word sentence. His instruction: "maybe we need another process that doesn't have a run-on sentence". Today the only gate is an expensive LLM reviewer that is spent AFTER the copy is written, and it lets mechanical faults through. This module is the cheap deterministic gate that runs FIRST and can be used to drive a revision loop before the LLM judge is called.

BUILD server/pipeline/content_mechanics.py as a dependency-free (stdlib only) library — NO model calls, NO network, NO file IO except what a caller passes in:

  check_mechanics(items) -> MechanicsReport
      `items` is a sequence of {"name": str, "text": str} (a caller maps posts/show-notes/email into this).
      Returns a report object/dataclass with: ok (bool), violations (list of {name, rule, detail, excerpt}), and per_item stats.
      Rules, each a named module constant with a one-line rationale:
        MAX_SENTENCE_WORDS = 38          # 40+ word run-ons were the named rejection
        MIN_CONTRACTION_RATE = 0.004     # zero contractions was the single biggest AI tell
        MAX_CTA_SIGNAL_TYPES = 1         # one ask per post; stacked asks were rejected
        MAX_CROSS_ITEM_SIMILARITY = 0.5  # "one post at three lengths" was rejected
        MIN_SHARED_SENTENCE_WORDS = 8    # a shared 8+ word sentence is reuse, not an echo
        BANNED_TERMS = (...)             # corporate buzzwords + sales cliches; include at least:
              delve, dive into, unpack, leverage, utilize, optimize, robust, seamless, streamline,
              foster, cultivate, bolster, landscape, ecosystem, holistic, alignment, synergy,
              bandwidth, revolutionary, game-changing, cutting-edge, elevate, transform, unlock,
              comprehensive, passionate, "just checking in", "circling back", "touching base",
              "hope this email finds you well", "wanted to reach out", "I came across"
      Checks: SENTENCE_LENGTH, CONTRACTIONS (items over 25 words only), BANNED_TERMS, EM_DASH
      (U+2014 or a spaced hyphen used between clauses), SELF_ANSWERED_QUESTION (a '?' sentence
      followed by a sentence of <= 3 words), CTA_COUNT (distinct signal types: imperative
      listen/hear/watch/read/tune directive, a URL or {{placeholder}}, a direct audience question),
      CROSS_ITEM_REUSE (shared normalised sentence >= MIN_SHARED_SENTENCE_WORDS words, or Jaccard
      over 4-word shingles >= MAX_CROSS_ITEM_SIMILARITY), UNSOURCED_STAT (a quantifier opener
      "most/the majority of/nearly all/few" plus a population noun and outcome verb, with no digit
      and no attribution word like "research", "study", "survey", "cites", "according to").
      Empty items, or an items sequence with no non-blank text, MUST return ok=False with an
      explicit UNMEASURABLE violation — never ok=True. Silence is not a pass.

  split_run_on(sentence, max_words=MAX_SENTENCE_WORDS) -> list[str]
      A deterministic repair helper for the most common fault: split an over-long sentence at the
      best available boundary. Prefer splitting at ", and " / ", but " / ", so " / ", while " /
      "; " nearest the midpoint; fall back to the comma nearest the midpoint; if no boundary
      exists, return the sentence unchanged (never truncate, never invent words). Each returned
      fragment must be capitalised and terminally punctuated, and joining them must preserve every
      original word in order.

  revision_prompt(report) -> str
      Render the violations as a compact, imperative instruction block a generator can be re-fed
      ("Rewrite item 'linkedin': sentence 3 is 44 words, split it; add contractions; ..."). Pure
      string building, no model call.

TESTS (tests/test_content_mechanics_gate.py; at least 5). Use the owner's REAL rejected material as fixtures:
 (1) the real 44-word approved show-notes sentence ("He rebuilt his career as a travel optometrist licensed across Ontario, Manitoba, and Newfoundland, and is now assembling a team of travel ODs to address Canada's multi-provincial doctor shortage while speaking and writing about careers that fit the life you actually want.") is flagged by SENTENCE_LENGTH, and split_run_on turns it into two sentences that together preserve every word in order, each under the limit;
 (2) "What made it possible? Burnout." is flagged SELF_ANSWERED_QUESTION;
 (3) "Most doctors who burn out leave optometry and don't come back." is flagged UNSOURCED_STAT, while "The research Fred cites says 54% of US optometrists face some level of burnout." is NOT flagged (attribution plus a digit);
 (4) NEGATIVE: a clean, contraction-rich, single-CTA, distinct post set returns ok=True with zero violations — proving the gate is not a blanket rejecter;
 (5) NEGATIVE: empty items and an all-blank item both return ok=False with UNMEASURABLE;
 (6) two items sharing a 10-word sentence are flagged CROSS_ITEM_REUSE;
 (7) a post with a listen directive AND a link AND an audience question is flagged CTA_COUNT;
 (8) revision_prompt output mentions every violating item name.
tasks.verified: deterministic mechanics gate plus a run-on splitter, red-proved on the owner's real rejected copy
